decision: Decide whether to authorize further analysis and a small pilot; not to execute trades today.
objective: Seek CPI + 4% net of estimated costs over rolling five-year periods; this is an objective, not a guarantee.
benchmark: 60% broad global equities / 40% U.S. investment-grade bonds
risk_measure: Unresolved. Before optimization proceeds, the CIO must clarify the enforcement rule for the 10% calendar-year-loss statement and select the optimization tradeoff. No risk-measure convention has been specified.
constraints: Distribute $750,000 at the end of each calendar quarter.
Keep at least 12 months of scheduled distributions ($3 million) in cash or daily-liquid government securities.
Long-only; no borrowing, short sales, or derivatives.
No single issuer may exceed 8% of the portfolio.
Annual turnover should not exceed 25% without documented committee approval.
At least 90% of the portfolio must be redeemable within five business days under ordinary market conditions.
validation_tests: Compare proposed-policy results with the stated 60/40 benchmark.
Compare with the cash-reserve-plus-60/40 naïve baseline.
Test weaker returns, higher inflation, and distribution needs.
Use a separate historical period from the one used to design assumptions.
Measure whether estimated trading and implementation costs prevent meeting the net objective.
Stop or escalate if the approach violates any hard constraint, fails liquidity or distribution requirements, or relies on an undefined interpretation of the 10% loss statement.
unresolved_ambiguity: Before optimization proceeds, the CIO must clarify the 10% calendar-year-loss enforcement rule (absolute rule, probability target, or monitoring threshold with a corrective action) and which tradeoff controls when the return objective, liquidity needs, and loss statement conflict. The investable universe is also not defined.
